newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tongkah mulls listing more units.
newsitem.headline: Tongkah mulls listing more units.

text.p: Diversified Tongkah Holdings Bhd is considering listing shares of its manufacturing units, and may later make a similar move for its increasingly dominant financial service businesses, its chief executive officer said.

The company, headed by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's second son, Mokhzani Mahathir, announced last week it was seeking an initial public offering (IPO) for its THB Industries Bhd unit, which makes precision tools.

"The listing of THBI will take care of five companies within that (manufacturing) group," Mokhzani said in an interview with Reuters on Monday. Mokhzani, who is also executive chairman of Tongkah, controls about 13 percent of the firm.
Offering shares in Tongkah's dispersed businesses would help investors get a better grasp of its investment value, he said.
"If you look at Tongkah Holdings and try to figure out where in Tongkah to invest your money, you can look at the quoted companies within the group," the 35-year-old Mokhzani said.
Tongkah has three core divisions -- financial services, manufacturing and medical services -- that encompass companies ranging from the Internet to laundry services.

Manufacturing is its most mature division, and units like Tongkah Moulding Technologies are "ready for listing on the Second Board", Mokhzani said, referring to the small-capitalisation index of the Kuala Lumpur share market.
Tongkah Moulding makes plastic injection moulds. Other manufacturing units make printed circuit boards, polished granite and automated machines.
A financial services unit IPO may take a little more time, he said. Tongkah is just building up the division, having acquired a majority stake in stockbroker Kestrel Securities Sdn Bhd in late 1995.

Tongkah is now in a proposed 84.48 million ringgit ($33.52 million) purchase of 88 percent of Perdana Finance Bhd. Marrying the two institutions will make the financial division the biggest unit in the Tongkah group as measured by paid-up capital, which will rise to 200 million ringgit from 30 million.
Perdana Finance will serve as a financing vehicle for Kestrel, reducing the interest costs that the stockbroker now pays for credit lines given to its customers.
"Last year we paid interest for credit lines (from other institutions) of four to five million ringgit. We'd rather pass it on to a company that is ours," Mokhzani said.
Asked about stock listings of the finance division, he said: "We might look at that three or four years down the line."

Tongkah's other large division is medical, which includes a 21 percent stake in listed Hospital Pantai Bhd and 51 percent stake in Tongkah Medivest Sdn Bhd, which provides clinical waste management and hospital laundry services.

Its 70 percent-owned Internet services provider THB Asia Connect Sdn Bhd was initially started because Tongkah needed an efficient computerised system to keep track of its work for a big hospital contract, Mokhzani said.
After this year's spate of acquisitions, Tongkah is likely to focus next year on building up its existing businesses, Mokhzani said.
For the year ended June 30, 1996, Tongkah reported a 34.20 percent rise in operating profit to 25 million ringgit and a 16.4 percent gain in turnover to 528.08 million ringgit.
The company does not provide a breakdown of division contributions, but Mokhzani said the financial division should contribute the lion's share of profits, with manufacturing dominating turnover.
